vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0283.md:29-57 Section 208.9 covers permanent nonstructural components, equipment, attachments, anchorages, required bracing, equipment exemptions, approved standards, and the rule that friction from gravity load is not seismic resistance.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0283.md:61-99 Section 208.9.2 defines total design lateral seismic force Fp and uses component amplification and response modification factors from Table 208-13 or dynamic properties.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0284.md:5-18 Section 208.9.3 requires members and connections transferring component forces to seismic-resisting systems to be designed for those forces and critical horizontal loading.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0286.md:11-57 Table 208-13 lists electrical, mechanical, plumbing, emergency power supply, essential communications, battery rack, and fuel tank equipment categories.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0286.md:63-65 Light fixtures and mechanical services installed in metal suspension systems must be independently supported from the structure above.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0287.md:10-18 Equipment examples include boilers, chillers, heat exchangers, pumps, air-handling units, cooling towers, control panels, motors, switchgear, transformers, life-safety equipment, major conduit, ducting, piping, and fire sprinkler systems.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0287.md:20-62 Seismic restraints may be omitted from selected piping, ducts, and raceways only when listed damage, support, fragility, and motion conditions are satisfied; flexible accommodation is required across different buildings or structural systems.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0287.md:64-79 Vibration isolators supporting equipment must be designed for lateral loads or restrained from lateral displacement and vertical uplift; vibration-isolated equipment uses ap/Rp = 2.5/1.5, and shallow or expansion anchors multiply anchor forces by 2.0.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0287.md:81-105 Equipment anchorage cannot rely on gravity friction; expansion anchors resisting tension are not used where operational vibrating loads are present; batteries and internal cabinet equipment require restraints.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0287.md:107-136 Design specifications for equipment must specify or reference design lateral forces and account for relative motion of attachments; alternative standards or test data are accepted only within stated minimum force boundaries.

vitruvius-connection/002_Raw-Conversion-Layer/006-Structural/NSCP-2015-7th-Edition/pages/page-0290.md:64-115 Buildings in flood hazard areas must resist flood hazards and use the most restrictive applicable flood hazard area; dry floodproofing includes utility and sanitary facilities made watertight and impermeable.
